statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail risk of 24% sits at the top of the watch band, one point below the 25% block threshold.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state is WATCH. The evidence-based danger window runs from the 12:30Z September employment report through 15:00Z, covering post-release repricing, the 13:30Z cash open and the first full cash hour. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ takes out a two-hour-old session high and extends to 31,105.50 after September payrolls undershoot at +29,000 and the 10-year yield sets a 5.154% session low
body: NQ futures trade 31,071.50 (+311.00, +1.01%) on a quote timed 12:32:03Z, inside a session range of 30,760.25-31,105.50 against a 30,760.50 prior settlement, from a 30,771.25 open on about 109.9k contracts. The decisive observation this hour is that the 31,035.25 session high, which had stood unchanged through the two preceding assessments, was taken out after the 12:30Z employment report and extended to 31,105.50. Price now sits 34.00 points, or 0.11%, beneath that new extreme, against 30,981.00 (+0.72%) timed 12:29:21Z with the old high still intact just before the release. Holding near the session extreme was the single live Tail amplifier absent from the last two publications, and it is present again. The September employment report undershot materially. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported total nonfarm payroll employment up 29,000 against a consensus near 84,000-90,000, with the unemployment rate rising to 4.2% from 4.1% where it had been expected to hold, and 7.1 million people unemployed. Average hourly earnings rose 5 cents, or 0.1%, to $37.81, trimming annual growth to 3.0% against roughly 3.2% expected. The prior two months were revised 60,000 lower in combination, July from +21,000 to -10,000 and August from +162,000 to +133,000. Health care added 17,000, construction 11,000 and manufacturing 9,000 while financial activities lost 7,000; average weekly hours held at 34.4 and participation was little changed at 61.8%. The print also diverged from this week's ADP reading of +90,000 private jobs, which had beaten its own +68,000 consensus. Cross-asset evidence is aligned with the equity advance rather than against it, which is why the amplifier count rose. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.170%, down 0.068 from a 5.238% close, having set a 5.154% session low after the release and now sitting about 17 basis points below Thursday's 5.344% multidecade high inside a 3.926%-5.345% 52-week range. The 2-year is 4.773% against a 4.787% close, but that reading is timed 12:30:00Z, at the release instant, so it does not yet carry post-release repricing. VIX is 16.05, down 2.07% from 16.39 inside a 15.89-16.24 band, on a 12:24:31Z timestamp that also predates the print. ES futures at 7,785.25 (+0.79%) extended to their own 7,800.00 session high and sit 14.75 points under it, so the broad index confirms rather than diverges, and reported Dow futures strength near 0.9% points to broad participation. WTI is 89.78, down 3.33% from 92.87 near an 88.92 session low after trading as high as 93.51, with Brent reported in a 97-102 dollar band; falling crude is a disinflationary offset rather than a Tail amplifier. October hike pricing was pared further on the release while most traders still carry at least one 25 basis point hike by December. Tail rises four points to 24% at the top of the watch band and stays one point below the block threshold. The increase is earned by observed evidence rather than by the size of the surprise: a fresh extension through a high that had been flat for two hours, price holding within 0.11% of that extreme, and aligned yields, volatility and breadth. It stops short of the block band because the structure is minutes old and the specific pathological pattern this score measures, repeated extension after failed retracements, has not formed. No retracement has yet been tested, and an untested pullback is not a failed one. Volatility is also decaying rather than expanding. Under this provider's risk definition the magnitude of a Tier-1 surprise and the size of an initial impulse inform Stress and Confidence, not Tail, until an observed price path denies mean reversion. The 13:30Z cash open is the checkpoint that would settle the question: an opening auction that extends past 31,105.50 with pullbacks that fail would support the block band, while a confirmed retracement would argue the other way. Stress rises three points to 78% in the high band. A Tier-1 miss, a one percent index impulse and visible labour-market deterioration make the environment difficult, while a 5.17% long end that is falling rather than rising, a 3.3% crude decline and a VIX near 16 keep it short of the extreme band. Confidence is 89%. The evidence set is broad, current, and primary where it matters most: the BLS release itself with sector detail and revisions, a timed NQ quote with full range and volume, a cross-checked ES reading, a real-time 10-year carrying its post-release session low, the verified Thursday cash close and 52-week range, and a verified seven-day calendar. Three limitations are recorded rather than smoothed over. The quote feed used for NQ and ES runs roughly ten minutes behind, so the levels above are the most recent timed ticks rather than the live print, and moves reported slightly later in the hour were larger. The 2-year and VIX readings are timestamped at or before the release and therefore understate post-release repricing. The shared Finviz context file is unusable this run: its collection timestamp is 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, roughly three days past the 90-minute freshness limit, and its collection status is partial, so it contributed nothing and full independent research was performed in its place.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band. Tail opened the window at 20% in the 12:00Z hour on 1 October, peaked at 24% in the 14:00Z hour as long-end selling intensified, eased to 21% at 15:00Z, then printed 20% for fifteen consecutive hours across the U.S. afternoon and the Asian session before stepping to 21% at 07:00Z, 23% at 08:00Z and 22% at 09:00Z as the European-morning advance gained directional efficiency, and returning to 20% for the final two hours once a genuine retracement formed and the session high stopped extending. Stress ranged from 74% to a 79% overnight peak and closed the window at 75%; Confidence held between 87% and 89%. Only the 08:00Z and 09:00Z slots were published as trend-up; the other 22 hours were mixed.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 24% for the current 12:00Z hour on the observed post-release extension and keeps 24% through the 13:00Z hour containing the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:00Z first full cash hour, then eases to 23% at 15:00Z and to 21% by late afternoon as repricing is assumed to complete. No slot reaches the 25% block threshold, because that would require observed repeated extension after failed retracements and no retracement has yet been tested; the escalation condition is named explicitly on each of those hours instead. A small uplift to 22% covers the 19:00Z power hour before Tail returns to the 20% watch floor at the 20:00Z cash close. CME equity index futures settle for the weekend at 21:00Z, so the final fifteen slots carry an explicit 20% watch floor rather than a projection of structure: no price path can form inside a closed market. Stress peaks at 80% across the cash open, decays through the afternoon and settles on a 58% weekend floor held deliberately above a quiet-market reading because the 5.17% long end and the active Middle East conflict persist across the halt. Confidence steps down from 89% to 73% with distance from the evidence cutoff.

forecast.analysis: Observed: September payrolls printed +29,000 against an +84,000-90,000 consensus with unemployment up to 4.2%, and NQ took out its two-hour-old 31,035.25 high, extending to 31,105.50 and holding 0.11% below it. The 10-year set a 5.154% session low. Aligned amplifiers are present, but no retracement has yet been tested.
drivers: September payrolls +29,000 against an +84,000-90,000 consensus
Session high extended from 31,035.25 to 31,105.50 after the release
NQ holding 0.11% below the new session extreme
10-year at a 5.154% session low; ES also set a new session high
No retracement tested yet, so failed-pullback structure is unestablished

forecast.analysis: The 13:30Z cash open is this hour's checkpoint and Tail holds at the top of the watch band at 24%. An opening auction that extends past the 31,105.50 session high with pullbacks that fail would complete the pattern this score measures and justify the block band; a confirmed retracement would invalidate that path.
drivers: 13:30Z U.S. cash open auction is this hour's decisive checkpoint
Extension past 31,105.50 with failing pullbacks is the amplifier to watch
A confirmed retracement would invalidate the escalation path
Dovish repricing could instead sustain a one-way relief advance

forecast.analysis: First full cash hour, with August Factory Orders at 14:00Z as a secondary release. Tail stays at 24% conditional on opening-range two-way trade. The pathological case is repeated extension after failed retracements once the opening auction completes; that structure has not formed and remains an assumption rather than an observation.
drivers: August Factory Orders at 14:00Z is a secondary scheduled checkpoint
Opening-range behaviour decides whether extension persists
Conditional risk: repeated extension after failed retracements

forecast.analysis: Repricing is assumed largely complete by this hour, so Tail eases to 23%. A dovish payroll outcome that holds the long end below Thursday's 5.344% multidecade peak would normally support orderly two-way trade. The residual risk case is a sustained afternoon leg that denies retracement.
drivers: Post-release price discovery assumed substantially complete
Long end holding below Thursday's 5.344% multidecade high
Residual risk: a sustained afternoon directional leg

news.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq stage comeback as Treasury yields fall, chip stocks gain

forecast.analysis: Tail eases to 22% because the mid-afternoon normally carries the session's lowest event density. Friday positioning ahead of the weekend futures halt can thin liquidity, which raises slippage risk more than it raises mean-reversion failure risk. No structure is observed for this hour.
drivers: Lowest scheduled-event density of the cash session
Pre-weekend positioning can thin depth without creating one-way structure
Unobserved hour: these scores are conditional

forecast.analysis: Tail reaches the 21% lower watch band. By this hour the payroll reaction is assumed priced and volatility decay is the base case, consistent with VIX entering the session at 16.08. A renewed long-end move back toward 5.30% is the main condition that would argue for a higher reading.
drivers: Volatility decay is the base case once the release is priced
Condition for escalation: long end back toward 5.30%
VIX entered the session at 16.08, in the lower part of its range

forecast.analysis: Tail holds 21%. This hour has no index-relevant scheduled catalyst, and the 17:00Z Baker Hughes rig count is a low-impact oil datapoint rather than an index driver. Stress continues to decay because the crude decline and the easing long end both reduce active stress channels.
drivers: No index-relevant scheduled release in this hour
Crude decline and easing long end reduce active stress channels
WTI near an 88.92 session low after a 3.3% fall

news.title: EU says oil reserve release possible amid US pressure

forecast.analysis: Tail lifts to 22% for the power hour, where month-start rebalancing and pre-weekend squaring can produce a late directional leg. The uplift reflects a recurring liquidity pattern, not observed structure. A late one-way close that denies retracement is the specific conditional risk.
drivers: Power-hour rebalancing and pre-weekend squaring can force a late leg
Conditional risk: a late one-way close without retracement
Uplift reflects a liquidity pattern, not observed structure

forecast.analysis: Tail returns to the 20% watch floor at the 20:00Z cash close and Stress falls to 68% as the session ends and the scheduled event set empties. The residual risk for this hour is a closing imbalance rather than a sustained trend, which is a slippage and gap concern more than a path concern.
drivers: 20:00Z U.S. cash close empties the scheduled event set
Closing imbalance is a slippage risk, not a trend risk

forecast.analysis: CME equity index futures settle for the weekend at 21:00Z, so this hour contains the transition into a closed market. The 20% reading is an explicitly carried watch floor rather than a projection of structure: once the venue is shut no price path can form and no mean-reversion failure can occur.
drivers: CME equity index futures halt for the weekend at 21:00Z
Carried watch floor, not a structural projection
No price path can form inside a closed market

forecast.analysis: First full hour of the weekend halt. Stress steps to 58% in the elevated band, held deliberately above a quiet-market reading because the 5.19% long end and the active Middle East conflict persist across the closure and transmit through the reopening gap rather than through this hour.
drivers: First full closed hour: no venue and no price discovery
Stress held above a quiet reading for persistent long-end and conflict risk
Risk transmits through the Sunday reopening gap, not this hour

forecast.analysis: Second full closed hour. Weekend headline accumulation begins here: EU and IEA deliberations over a coordinated reserve release, and any Middle East escalation, can develop with no venue in which to price them. Confidence steps down with distance from the evidence cutoff.
drivers: Weekend headline risk accumulates with no venue to price it
EU and IEA reserve deliberations remain an open thread
Confidence decays with distance from the evidence cutoff

news.title: EU says oil reserve release possible amid US pressure

forecast.analysis: Saturday UTC begins with futures shut and the next price discovery not due until the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, which lies beyond this 24-hour horizon. The carried 20% floor therefore describes policy continuity across a closed market rather than any assessed Saturday price path.
drivers: Saturday UTC begins with equity index futures shut
Next price discovery is the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, beyond this horizon
Carried floor expresses policy continuity, not an assessed path

forecast.analysis: Closed market in the early Saturday UTC hours. With no exchange, no quote and no possible retracement, the Tail definition has nothing to measure. The reading stays at the watch floor rather than moving to a green state because the resumption gap, not this hour, carries the genuine risk.
drivers: No exchange and no quote: the Tail definition has nothing to measure
Watch floor preferred to a green state because of resumption-gap risk

forecast.analysis: Closed market. The September payroll miss will be digested over the weekend by research and rate-strategy desks, and any shift in October and December hike pricing surfaces at the Sunday reopen. This hour itself carries no structure and no observable mean-reversion behaviour.
drivers: Weekend digestion of the payroll miss shifts rate pricing off-venue
October and December hike pricing resets at the reopen
No observable structure inside a closed hour

forecast.analysis: Closed market. Confidence continues its scheduled decay because every observation behind this forecast predates the assessment cutoff, and a Saturday hour more than fourteen hours past that cutoff is supported by no fresh evidence at all. These scores are carried, not re-derived from new data.
drivers: All evidence behind this slot predates the assessment cutoff
Scores are carried rather than re-derived

forecast.analysis: Closed market. The next scheduled index-relevant catalyst is ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z on 5 October, which sits outside this horizon. Nothing between this hour and the reopen can create the persistent directional path that the Tail score is defined to measure.
drivers: Next index catalyst is ISM Services on 5 October, outside this horizon
No mechanism inside the closure can create a persistent path

forecast.analysis: Closed market. The long end stood near 5.19% at the Friday assessment cutoff, after a quarter described as the bond market's worst in decades. That backdrop is the main reason the weekend Stress floor stays in the elevated band instead of falling to a quiet-market level.
drivers: Long end near 5.19% at the cutoff, after the worst bond quarter in decades
Backdrop justifies an elevated rather than quiet weekend Stress floor

forecast.analysis: Closed market on Saturday morning UTC. Asian venues are shut as well, so there is no cross-asset tape available to confirm or contradict Friday's dovish repricing. Partial-evidence conditions like this are exactly where a carried floor is more truthful than a re-derived score.
drivers: Asian venues also shut: no confirming cross-asset tape
A carried floor is more truthful than a re-derived score here

forecast.analysis: Closed market. Crude is the one genuinely unresolved weekend thread, with Brent reported in a 97-102 dollar band and a coordinated reserve release still under discussion. A weekend decision would transmit to equities through the reopening gap, not through this hour.
drivers: Brent in a 97-102 dollar band with a reserve release under discussion
A weekend decision transmits through the reopening gap

forecast.analysis: Closed market. Confidence has stepped to 75% at the lower edge of the high band, which records the roughly twenty-hour distance from the evidence cutoff rather than any deterioration in the quality of the research actually gathered on Friday morning.
drivers: Confidence records distance from the cutoff, not weaker research
Roughly twenty hours past the Friday observation set

forecast.analysis: Closed market. Tail stays at the 20% watch floor for a twelfth consecutive closed hour. Holding the level flat is deliberate: manufacturing variation across hours in which no market exists would misrepresent a carried policy state as an assessed price-path judgement.
drivers: Twelfth consecutive closed hour at the carried watch floor
A flat level avoids dressing a carry as an assessed judgement

forecast.analysis: Closed market in the late Saturday morning UTC hours. The practical question for the resumption is whether Friday's dovish repricing extends or reverses once liquidity returns, and that is a Sunday-evening question which sits beyond the final slot of this forecast.
drivers: Resumption question: does Friday's dovish repricing extend or reverse
That question resolves after this forecast horizon ends

forecast.analysis: Final slot of the horizon, with futures still shut. The forecast ends inside the weekend closure, so the last reading is a carried watch floor rather than a judgement about tradeable structure. The next published assessment will re-derive its scores from fresh evidence.
drivers: Horizon ends inside the weekend closure
The next assessment re-derives scores from fresh evidence
